Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — The npm Threat Landscape: Attack Surface and Mitigations (Updated June 2)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm/node lifecycle script fetching Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun · [LLM] Malicious @bitwarden/cli payload artifacts on disk (bw_setup.js, bw1.js, Shai-Hulud markers)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 beacon to audit.checkmarx[.]cx /v1/telemetry (TeamPCP Shai-Hulud Third Coming) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
npm/node lifecycle script fetching Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun AIInstallation High
Detects an npm preinstall/postinstall lifecycle script (node.exe parented by npm) reaching out to github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases to download the Bun v1.3.13 runtime. This is the exact bootstrap behaviour of the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 payload (bw_setup.js Stage-1) and is highly anomalous on developer endpoints because legitimate JS projects rarely pull Bun via a package-install hook. Rationale: Article explicitly names github.com/oven-sh/bun and Bun v1.3.13 as the runtime downloaded by Stage-1 bw_setup.js during npm preinstall — pairing the github.com/oven-sh/bun URL token with an npm-family parent process is a near-zero-FP signature on production endpoints (developer laptops will produce occasional FPs, hence the parent-process pinning). Cross-checked against Socket and Checkmarx advisories listed below. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain • https://checkmarx.com/blog/checkmarx-supply-chain-incident-april-2026/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer intentionally installing Bun via an npm/yarn install script on a workstation
  • CI/CD build agent (GitHub Actions/Jenkins) running 'curl ... github.com/oven-sh/bun/install.sh | bash' in a job
  • Internal devtool wrapper that bootstraps a Bun toolchain on first run
  • Open-source project benchmark suites that download Bun in their install step
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "jenkins" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "runner\\_work" and DeviceName !startswith "build-" and DeviceName !startswith "ci-" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "\\actions-runner\\"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Pull the full process tree (npm/node parent → downloader child → Bun URL) and the downloaded artifact's SHA256. Check whether the package the user just installed is on the published TeamPCP IOC list (@bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 and any sibling Checkmarx packages). Inspect npm cache (~/.npm/_cacache and %AppData%\npm-cache) for the offending package and its preinstall script. Step 2 — Contain: Isolate the host, rotate every credential reachable from it (npm tokens, GitHub PATs, cloud CLI creds, SSH keys, .env secrets, Docker/kubeconfig), revoke any GitHub PAT touched in the last 30 days, and block egress to audit.checkmarx[.]cx + 94.154.172[.]43 at the perimeter. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot on the user's npm/GitHub identity for new public repos containing the string 'Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming', then sweep the org for any other host that downloaded github.com/oven-sh/bun via an npm parent in the last 30 days.
let bunUrlIndicators = dynamic(["github.com/oven-sh/bun", "oven-sh/bun/releases", "bun-windows-x64", "bun-linux-x64", "bun-darwin"]);
let npmParents = dynamic(["npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe"]);
let downloaderChildren = dynamic(["node.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","pwsh.exe"]);
// Process-tree pivot — npm parent spawning a downloader child with Bun URL on the command line
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (npmParents) or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (npmParents)
    | where FileName in~ (downloaderChildren)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              InitImage  = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitCmd    = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildImage = FileName,
              ChildCmd   = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
// Network pivot — same process families connecting to github.com for the Bun release tarball
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where RemoteUrl has "github.com" and (RemoteUrl has "oven-sh/bun" or RemoteUrl has "bun-windows" or RemoteUrl has "bun-linux" or RemoteUrl has "bun-darwin")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (downloaderChildren)
    | where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (npmParents) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              InitImage   = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitCmd     = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildImage  = "<network-egress>", ChildCmd = RemoteUrl, SHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256;
union ProcHits, NetHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let bunUrlIndicators = dynamic(["github.com/oven-sh/bun", "oven-sh/bun/releases", "bun-windows-x64", "bun-linux-x64", "bun-darwin"]);
let npmParents = dynamic(["npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe","npm","node","yarn","pnpm","npx"]);
let downloaderChildren = dynamic(["node.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","wget.exe","bun.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","pwsh.exe","node","curl","wget","bun","bash","sh","pwsh"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any (downloaderChildren) or ParentProcessName has_any (downloaderChildren)
| where (ParentProcessName has_any (npmParents) or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents) or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (npmParents))
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators) or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (bunUrlIndicators)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: NPM Lifecycle Script Downloading Bun Runtime from oven-sh GitHub
id: 4c2f6f8a-9d1e-4b8c-9a3f-2e8a0b1c4d51
status: experimental
description: Detects an npm/yarn/pnpm install lifecycle script (Node.js parented by npm) spawning a downloader to fetch the Bun JavaScript runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun — the Stage-1 bootstrap of the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli supply-chain payload.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/
  - https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
  selection_url:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'github.com/oven-sh/bun'
      - 'oven-sh/bun/releases'
      - 'bun-windows-x64'
      - 'bun-linux-x64'
      - 'bun-darwin'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_url
falsepositives:
  - Developer manually upgrading the Bun runtime via an automation script
  - CI agent installing Bun in a build pipeline (scope detection to dev workstations or scope out CI hosts)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\npm.exe OR *\NPM.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\NODE.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\npx.exe) @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\CURL.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\bun.exe) @CommandLine:(*github.com/oven-sh/bun* OR *oven-sh/bun/releases* OR *bun-windows-x64* OR *bun-linux-x64* OR *bun-darwin*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|node|yarn|pnpm|npx)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(node|curl|powershell|pwsh|wget|bun|bash|sh)\.exe$/i

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

C2 beacon to audit.checkmarx[.]cx /v1/telemetry (TeamPCP Shai-Hulud Third Coming) AICommand & Control High
Detects any outbound network/DNS activity to the TeamPCP C2 audit.checkmarx[.]cx (94.154.172.43) — particularly POSTs to the /v1/telemetry path — that exfiltrates harvested cloud, CI/CD and developer credentials from compromised hosts. The domain visually impersonates Checkmarx's legitimate infrastructure but resolves to attacker-controlled space. Rationale: Article Table 1 names the C2 server, IP and HTTP path explicitly (audit.checkmarx[.]cx:443 / 94.154.172.43 / /v1/telemetry) — any hit on these three indicators is a confirmed-compromise signal, not a hunting hypothesis. Corroborated by Checkmarx's official disclosure that all four artifact families (npm, Docker Hub, GitHub Actions, VS Code) shared this C2. Cross-checked against: • https://checkmarx.com/blog/checkmarx-supply-chain-incident-april-2026/ • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security analyst manually visiting the domain during IR triage (filter on known analyst workstation/jump-host)
  • Threat-intel sandbox or scanner deliberately resolving the IOC (e.g. a TI enrichment service hosted on the corporate network)
  • Outbound proxy/DLP solution generating a synthetic resolution for the indicator feed
  • Endpoint EDR sensor itself pulling the indicator for local matching (filter on MsSense.exe / SenseIR.exe)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","SenseIR.exe","MsMpEng.exe") and DeviceName !in~ ("soc-jump-01","ir-analyst-vm")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Pull every host that resolved audit.checkmarx[.]cx or connected to 94.154.172.43 in the last 30 days; for each, identify the initiating process and user. Capture the full HTTPS request body if proxy decryption is available — POST to /v1/telemetry carries exfiltrated tokens. Step 2 — Contain: Block audit.checkmarx[.]cx and 94.154.172.43 at DNS, proxy and firewall. Force-rotate every npm token, GitHub PAT, AWS/GCP/Azure CLI credential, Docker Hub token and .env-stored secret on every connecting host within the last 24h. Step 3 — Hunt: For each affected user, list every npm package and GitHub repo they own — TeamPCP's worm republishes packages and creates public 'Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming' repos under the victim identity. Pivot to UC #3 (file artifacts) and UC #1 (Bun download).
let c2Hosts = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx", "audit.checkmarx[.]cx"]);
let c2Ips    = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let c2Path   = "/v1/telemetry";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (RemoteUrl has_any (c2Hosts)) or (RemoteIP in (c2Ips)) or (RemoteUrl has c2Path and RemotePort in (443, 80))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","SenseIR.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2Hosts = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
let c2Ips    = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let c2Path   = "/v1/telemetry";
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstHostname has_any (c2Hosts) or DstIpAddr in (c2Ips) or (isnotempty(Url) and Url has c2Path and DstPortNumber in (443, 80))
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkApplicationProtocol
),
(
  ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (c2Hosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsQueryTypeName, DnsResponseCodeName
),
(
  ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where HttpHostName has_any (c2Hosts) or Url has c2Path and (HttpHostName has "checkmarx.cx")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, HttpHostName, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (c2Hosts) or DestinationIP in (c2Ips) or RequestURL has "audit.checkmarx.cx" or RequestURL has c2Path
  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious @bitwarden/cli payload artifacts on disk (bw_setup.js, bw1.js, Shai-Hulud markers) AIInstallation High
Detects creation or execution of the Stage-1 (bw_setup.js) and Stage-2 (bw1.js) Node.js scripts dropped by the TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 npm package, as well as the 'Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming' string written into public repo content that the worm uses as an attribution marker and propagation beacon. This catches both the install-time drop on the npm install path and any post-compromise replay. Rationale: Article explicitly names bw_setup.js (Stage-1 bootstrap, registered as the `bw` bin) and bw1.js (Stage-2 Bun payload) inside the malicious @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 package. The legitimate Bitwarden CLI ships neither filename, so the filename + package path combo is a hard-IOC match. The Shai-Hulud Third Coming string is a TeamPCP attribution marker per the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/teampcp-bitwarden-cli-supply-chain • https://github.com/bitwarden/clients/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546.016 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher unzipping a captured copy of the malicious package on an analyst workstation for analysis (filter on known analyst hosts)
  • Threat-intel ingestion pipeline downloading the package from npm cache for IOC extraction
  • SOC sandbox/detonation environment replaying the package install
  • Legitimate package named 'bw1.js' or 'bw_setup.js' shipped by an unrelated internal project (unlikely; verify against package.json)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "\\sandboxes\\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains "\\detonation\\" and DeviceName !startswith "ti-sandbox-" and DeviceName !startswith "malware-analysis-"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Capture the dropping process tree and the surrounding package.json — confirm version is 2026.4.0 and that the preinstall script invokes bw_setup.js. Hash bw1.js and submit to threat intel. Step 2 — Contain: Isolate host, run `npm uninstall -g @bitwarden/cli` and `npm cache clean --force`, wipe ~/.npm/_cacache, kill any lingering bun.exe / node.exe processes parented by npm, rotate all credentials reachable from the host (npm token, GitHub PAT, cloud CLI tokens, .env secrets, SSH keys). Step 3 — Hunt: Query the user's GitHub for any new public repository created in the last 30 days containing the string 'Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming' — this is the worm's propagation marker — and audit every npm package the user can publish for unauthorised releases.
let stageFiles = dynamic(["bw_setup.js", "bw1.js"]);
let packageHints = dynamic(["@bitwarden\\cli", "@bitwarden/cli", "node_modules\\@bitwarden\\cli", "node_modules/@bitwarden/cli"]);
let shaiHuludMarker = "Shai-Hulud: The Third Coming";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where (FileName in~ (stageFiles)) or (FolderPath has_any (packageHints) and FileName endswith ".js") or (AdditionalFields has shaiHuludMarker)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              FolderPath, FileName, SHA256;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (stageFiles)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
              FolderPath, FileName = FileName, SHA256, ProcCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let stageFiles = dynamic(["bw_setup.js", "bw1.js"]);
let packageHints = dynamic(["@bitwarden\\cli", "@bitwarden/cli", "node_modules\\@bitwarden\\cli", "node_modules/@bitwarden/cli"]);
let npmRunners = dynamic(["npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe","npm","node","yarn","pnpm","bun"]);
let FileHits = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (TargetFileName in~ (stageFiles)) or (TargetFilePath has_any (packageHints) and TargetFileExtension =~ "js")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256;
let ProcHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (npmRunners) or ParentProcessName has_any (npmRunners)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (stageFiles)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
              TargetFilePath = "", TargetFileName = "", TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP @bitwarden/cli Stage Payload File Drop (bw_setup.js / bw1.js)
id: 9a4d2c7e-3b6f-4e1a-8d2c-5f6a7b8e9d03
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of the Stage-1 (bw_setup.js) or Stage-2 (bw1.js) Node.js script files dropped by the malicious @bitwarden/cli@2026.4.0 npm package distributed by TeamPCP as part of the Shai-Hulud Third Coming supply-chain campaign.
references:

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Multiple redhat-cloud-services npm Packages compromised

StepSecurity
2026-06-02 10 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Several packages in the @redhat-cloud-services npm scope were found to carry malicious payloads that fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install. The affected versions span multiple packages across the RedHat Cloud Services frontend ecosystem. The payload is a sophisticated multi-stage credential harvester that targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, and CircleCI tokens

ATT&CKT1027 T1190 T1195.002

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Bun runtime download to /tmp from a node process during npm install · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Multiple redhat-cloud-services npm Packages compromised
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm preinstall hook executing oversized node index.js from @redhat-cloud-services package · [LLM] Bun spawned from npm install context executing /tmp/p*.js implant
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Process reading /proc/<pid>/mem of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker (in-memory secret extraction)
npm preinstall hook executing oversized node index.js from @redhat-cloud-services package AIInstallation High
Detects the entry point of the @redhat-cloud-services supply-chain compromise: a preinstall script firing node against an unusually large (>1 MB) index.js shipped inside an @redhat-cloud-services scoped package directory. The legitimate libraries in this scope have tiny entry files, so a 4.2 MB index.js executing during install is a near-deterministic signal of the malicious version. Rationale: Anchors on the exact preinstall execution string named in package.json (`node index.js`) combined with the scoped-package path `@redhat-cloud-services` and the article's distinguishing 4.2 MB size of index.js (vs <100 KB for legitimate releases). Cross-checked against the StepSecurity disclosure and the three RedHatInsights GitHub issues (#492, #2329, #57). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/javascript-clients/issues/492 • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/frontend-components/issues/2329 • https://github.com/RedHatInsights/platform-frontend-ai-toolkit/issues/57
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate RedHat dev tooling installs on engineer workstations once a clean version is republished — pin to the known-malicious versions in the affected-packages table
  • Internal mirrors that proxy the registry may still serve a cached malicious tarball after upstream removal
  • Security-team-controlled detonation sandboxes installing the bad versions intentionally for IR
  • CI re-runs from cached node_modules tarballs that pre-date the cleanup
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--dry-run","--ignore-scripts") or ProcessCommandLine has "--ignore-scripts")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm the installed package@version against the affected-packages table (e.g. host-inventory-client@5.0.3, types@3.6.1); pull the on-disk index.js size and SHA256; correlate with the GitHub Actions run / developer workstation identity. Step 2 — Contain: kill the node process; quarantine the host's node_modules; rotate every secret the host had access to (AWS, GCP, Azure, GitHub PATs, npm tokens, Vault, CircleCI, Kubernetes kubeconfigs); revoke OIDC-issued tokens minted during the window. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on UC2/UC3/UC4 for the same host; search registry-mirror access logs for the malicious versions being pulled by other workloads; review GitHub branch-protection bypass and any commits signed by the same OIDC identity during the install window.
let SuspectPackages = dynamic(["@redhat-cloud-services/types","@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components-utilities","@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components","@redhat-cloud-services/rbac-client","@redhat-cloud-services/javascript-clients-shared","@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components-config-utilities","@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components-notifications","@redhat-cloud-services/tsc-transform-imports","@redhat-cloud-services/frontend-components-config","@redhat-cloud-services/eslint-config-redhat-cloud-services","@redhat-cloud-services/host-inventory-client","@redhat-cloud-services/rule-components","@redhat-cloud-services/notifications-client","@redhat-cloud-services/chrome","@redhat-cloud-services/hcc-pf-mcp"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm","npm.exe","node","node.exe","yarn","pnpm","npx","npm-cli.js")
| where FileName in~ ("node","node.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "@redhat-cloud-services" and ProcessCommandLine has "index.js"
| extend MatchedPackage = tostring(set_difference(SuspectPackages, dynamic([])))
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FolderPath has "@redhat-cloud-services" and FileName =~ "index.js"
    | where FileSize > 1048576
    | summarize MaxSize = max(FileSize) by DeviceId, FolderPath
) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, MaxSize, MatchedPackage
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectScope = "@redhat-cloud-services";
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where Facility in ("user","daemon","kern") or ProcessName in ("auditd","audispd")
| where SyslogMessage has "node" and SyslogMessage has SuspectScope and SyslogMessage has "index.js"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("preinstall","npm install","npm-cli.js","npx","yarn","pnpm")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: npm preinstall executes oversized index.js from @redhat-cloud-services
id: 4f8a3c2d-9e1b-4a7c-8f60-1b9d2e3c4a51
description: Detects node executing an index.js inside a @redhat-cloud-services scoped package directory during npm install, the entry point of the June-2026 supply-chain compromise.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/multiple-redhat-cloud-services-npm-packages-compromised
author: SOC Detection Eng
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent_selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/npm'
      - '/node'
      - '/yarn'
      - '/pnpm'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
  child_selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '\node.exe'
  cmdline_selection:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '@redhat-cloud-services'
      - 'index.js'
  condition: parent_selection and child_selection and cmdline_selection
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*node*@redhat-cloud-services*index.js* OR *Node*@redhat-cloud-services*index.js*) AND (@process.parent.name:(npm OR node OR yarn OR pnpm OR npx) OR @process.command_line:(*preinstall* OR *"npm install"*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\/(node|node\.exe)$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(npm|node|yarn|pnpm|npx)(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("@redhat-cloud-services", field=CommandLine)
| regex("index\\.js", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

Bun runtime download to /tmp from a node process during npm install AIDelivery High
Detects Stage 3 of the redhat-cloud-services compromise: the in-memory _b downloader retrieves bun-v1.3.13 from the official Bun GitHub releases CDN and drops it into a randomly-named /tmp/ subdirectory, then registers it via globalThis.getBunPath. Article-specific because legitimate library installs never fetch a parallel JS runtime at install time. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact runtime version `bun-v1.3.13`, the GitHub releases CDN host (`objects.githubusercontent.com` is the actual blob host behind github.com release downloads), and the `/tmp/<random>/bun` drop path described in Stage 3. Pairs network event with the file-create within 5 minutes to suppress generic Bun installs on developer machines. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/bun-v1.3.13
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually running curl/bun installer to try Bun on a workstation
  • CI image-build steps that legitimately download Bun for a project that uses it (rare in RHEL/insights tooling)
  • Renovate/Dependabot autodeps tasks that exercise package install in sandboxes
  • Sysadmin troubleshooting a previously-cached corrupt Bun binary
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("package.json\"bun\"","bunfig.toml") or DeviceName has_any ("-bunlab-","-bunci-"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm the parent of the node download is an npm install of an @redhat-cloud-services package; capture the URL, the dropped /tmp/<random>/bun, and its SHA256. Step 2 — Contain: kill node, the Bun process, and any /tmp/p*.js it spawned; isolate the host; revoke any cloud / GitHub OIDC tokens issued to the runner. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot to UC3 (/proc/<pid>/mem reads by Bun) and UC4 (Bun executing /tmp/p*.js); look across the fleet for any other host that fetched bun-v1.3.13 from a node process — every hit is a likely-compromised CI runner.
let BunDownload = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","npm")
    | where (RemoteUrl has "github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases" or RemoteUrl has "bun-v1.3.13" or RemoteUrl has "objects.githubusercontent.com")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP;
let BunDrop = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" or FolderPath startswith "/var/folders/"
    | where FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","tar","unzip")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
BunDownload
| join kind=inner BunDrop on DeviceId
| where Timestamp1 between (Timestamp .. Timestamp + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, DropPath = strcat(FolderPath, FileName), InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let BunNet = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (Url has "github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases" or Url has "bun-v1.3.13" or DstHostname has "objects.githubusercontent.com")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm")
    | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Url, DstIpAddr;
let BunDrop = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated"
    | where TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/" or TargetFilePath startswith "/var/folders/"
    | where TargetFileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
    | project DropTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName;
BunNet
| join kind=inner BunDrop on DvcHostname
| where DropTime between (NetTime .. NetTime + 5m)
| project NetTime, DropTime, DvcHostname, Url, DstIpAddr, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by NetTime desc
source:linux.auditd ((@process.name:(node OR npm) AND @network.destination.domain:(*github.com OR *githubusercontent.com) AND @process.command_line:(*bun-v1.3.13* OR *oven-sh/bun*)) OR (@auditd.type:PATH AND @file.path:(/tmp/*/bun OR /tmp/*/bun.exe) AND @process.name:node))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^(github\.com|objects\.githubusercontent\.com)$/i ContextImageFileName=/\/(node|npm)$/i)
OR
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/^\/(tmp|var\/folders)\/[^\/]+\/bun(\.exe)?$/i ContextImageFileName=/\/(node|npm|tar|unzip)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port values(All_Traffic.user) as user values(All_Traffic.app) as app from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app IN ("node","node.exe","npm") (All_Traffic.url="*github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases*" OR All_Traffic.url="*bun-v1.3.13*" OR All_Traffic.dest="objects.githubusercontent.com") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_id | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | join type=left src [| tstats `summariesonly` values(Filesystem.file_path) as bun_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/*" (Filesystem.file_name="bun" OR Filesystem.file_name="bun.exe") by Filesystem.dest | rename Filesystem.dest as src] | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_port values(All_Traffic.user) as user values(All_Traffic.app) as app from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app IN ("node","node.exe","npm") (All_Traffic.url="*github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases*" OR All_Traffic.url="*bun-v1.3.13*" OR All_Traffic.dest="objects.githubusercontent.com") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_id | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | join type=left src [| tstats summariesonly=false values(Filesystem.file_path) as bun_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="/tmp/*" (Filesystem.file_name="bun" OR Filesystem.file_name="bun.exe") by Filesystem.dest | rename Filesystem.dest as src] | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Process reading /proc/<pid>/mem of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker (in-memory secret extraction) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the credential-harvesting core of the implant: reading /proc/<pid>/mem of the GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process to scrape secrets that the runner holds in memory but never writes to disk. This is exactly the activity the StepSecurity Harden-Runner screenshot in the article captured and is the technique the payload uses to evade Harden-Runner-style detections by reading rather than calling out. Rationale: Anchors on /proc/<pid>/mem — the exact /proc read the article's Harden-Runner process-events screenshot captures — combined with node/bun as the reader (the Stage 1 entry point and the Stage 3 downloaded runtime). Joins forward to DeviceProcessEvents on the target PID to confirm it is Runner.Worker, eliminating debugger / strace noise. Source: StepSecurity blog + image SCR-20260601-oxms.png in-article screenshot showing Runner.Worker /proc/mem read. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/007/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/multiple-redhat-cloud-services-npm-packages-compromised
ATT&CKT1003.007 T1552.001 T1212
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Node-based debugger or profiler legitimately attached to a worker for performance work
  • Systemd-coredump or abrt-hook-ccpp reading process memory during a crash dump (different parent, usually root-owned)
  • Custom observability agent written in node that reads /proc to monitor RSS (verify by image hash / installed-package source)
  • SRE running strace -p / gdb -p against the runner during incident response
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("gdb","strace","perf record","abrt-hook-ccpp","systemd-coredump") or AccountName == "root" and InitiatingProcessFileName == "systemd-coredump")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine and parent tree of the node/bun reader; confirm the target PID is Runner.Worker by joining to process-create events; capture /tmp/<random>/bun SHA256. Step 2 — Contain: kill the node and bun processes; isolate the runner; revoke the runner's GitHub Actions OIDC tokens and every workflow secret the job had access to (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_*, GCP_*, AZURE_*, NPM_TOKEN, VAULT_TOKEN, CIRCLE_TOKEN, KUBECONFIG); rotate any long-lived keys downstream actions chained to. Step 3 — Hunt: search the fleet for any other process reading /proc/<pid>/mem of Runner.Worker (different package may share the same TTP); review last 30 days of GitHub Actions secret usage from those workflows; audit all artifacts produced by jobs that ran this implant.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileAccessed","FileCreated")
| where FolderPath startswith "/proc/" and FileName == "mem"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun")
| extend TargetPid = extract(@"/proc/(\d+)/", 1, FolderPath)
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName has_any ("Runner.Worker","Runner.Listener")
    | project DeviceId, TargetPid = tostring(ProcessId), RunnerCmd = ProcessCommandLine, RunnerName = FileName
) on DeviceId, TargetPid
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, TargetPid, RunnerName, RunnerCmd
| order by Timestamp desc
let ProcMemRe = @"/proc/\d+/mem";
let RunnerHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where SyslogMessage matches regex ProcMemRe
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("node", "bun")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
let AsimHits = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where TargetFilePath matches regex ProcMemRe
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node", "bun")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath;
union isfuzzy=true RunnerHits, AsimHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Bun spawned from npm install context executing /tmp/p*.js implant AIInstallation High
Detects Stage 3→4 handoff: the freshly downloaded /tmp/<random>/bun binary executes a randomly-named /tmp/p<random>.js file containing the AES-decrypted main payload. Combination of Bun residing in /tmp/, being invoked by a node process whose CWD is inside an npm install, and immediately running a /tmp/p*.js is article-specific and effectively never benign. Rationale: Anchors on three article-specific shapes that compose into a near-zero-FP signal: Bun binary path under /tmp/<random>/bun (Stage 3 drop), parent in (node, npm, bun) (Stage 1 / Stage 3 chain), child commandline matching /tmp/p<random>.js (Stage 4 implant file). Each alone is noisy; together they reproduce the Stage 3→4 handoff in the StepSecurity write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/multiple-redhat-cloud-services-npm-packages-compromised • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1140/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1140 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer hand-running `bun /tmp/playground.js` from a tutorial — different filename shape, won't match /tmp/p<random>.js
  • CI cache step that materialises a build artifact under /tmp/p* and runs it (verify by parent process and signed-by metadata)
  • Node test-runner that uses ephemeral /tmp files but with deterministic names (jest-*, mocha-*) — won't match the p<random> pattern
  • Renovate/dependency-update sandbox using its own tarball install — typically not Bun-mediated
Suppression filter
| where not (AccountName == "root" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("systemd","snapd")) and not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--test","--inspect","jest","mocha"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: capture full process tree (npm → node → bun chain), the SHA256 of /tmp/<random>/bun and /tmp/p<random>.js; preserve both files for IR. Step 2 — Contain: kill bun and any child it spawned; isolate the host / runner; revoke every workflow secret + every cloud token (AWS / GCP / Azure / GitHub OIDC / npm / Vault / CircleCI / Kubernetes) the runner had access to; tear down the runner VM rather than reuse. Step 3 — Hunt: dump and reverse /tmp/p<random>.js to identify the C2 domain (article notes the B5 cipher with password ba2c6ddb3672bdd6a611e6850b4f700b52aed3dab2f1b3d5f8c839d4a157a709 and salt 5b26508dc0f1075a7c0b4d8aa464487e — once decrypted, sweep DNS for that domain); pivot to UC2/UC3 hits on the same host; audit GitHub Actions runs for all affected packages.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" and FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")) or (InitiatingProcessFolderPath startswith "/tmp/" and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","npm","bun")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/p[A-Za-z0-9]+\.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TmpJsRe = @"/tmp/p[A-Za-z0-9]+\.js";
let AsimHits = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (ActingProcessName endswith "/bun" or ActingProcessName endswith "/node" or ActingProcessName endswith "/npm")
    | where TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex TmpJsRe or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex TmpJsRe
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine;
let SyslogHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where SyslogMessage matches regex TmpJsRe
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("bun", "node")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
union isfuzzy=true AsimHits, SyslogHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc

| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession

            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber

| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Laravel-Lang Supply Chain Attack: Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten to Steal CI Secrets

StepSecurity
2026-06-02 9 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

On May 22, 2026, an attacker with push access to the Laravel-Lang GitHub organization rewrote every git tag across multiple popular Composer packages within a single 15 minute window. Anyone running composer update or installing fresh against laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/actions, or laravel-lang/attributes now pulls a payload that exfiltrates CI secrets to a typosquatted attacker domain. StepSecurity confirmed end to end exploitation in an isolated runner and has filed security issues in all four repositories.

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002
Domainsflipboxstudio.info
SHA1a5ea2e8fa92ccf29… 50ac0db454d19234… c45764e70285146d… a9f8d88cf98e3598… bba2e443dc7ff1f8…

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] GitHub bulk git tag force-push by single actor across multiple org repos
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PHP CLI drops hidden /tmp dropper artefacts (Laravel-Lang autoload payload) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Laravel-Lang Supply Chain Attack: Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Re
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Egress to typosquatted C2 flipboxstudio.info (Laravel-Lang Composer SC) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Orphaned process (ppid=1) executing from /tmp hidden hex path (post-dropper stage-2)
Egress to typosquatted C2 flipboxstudio.info (Laravel-Lang Composer SC) AICommand & Control High
Hunts DNS or HTTP(S) callbacks to flipboxstudio.info, the attacker-controlled typosquat of the legitimate flipboxstudio.com used as the stage-1 fetch endpoint (/payload) and stage-2 exfiltration sink (/exfil) by the May 2026 Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain dropper. Single-IOC alerter — exact-domain match, near-zero FP expectation. Rationale: Anchors on the exact attacker-controlled domain `flipboxstudio.info` named verbatim in the IOC block as both the stage-1 GET endpoint (/payload) and stage-2 POST exfil endpoint (/exfil). The domain is a brand-new typosquat of flipboxstudio.com with no legitimate business use — any hit is high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1568.002 T1041
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel scanner or sandbox detonating the IOC from a corporate egress IP
  • Researcher manually visiting the article and clicking through to the live domain
  • Defensive SOAR playbook auto-fetching the URL for hash extraction
  • Backup/mirror service crawling Composer registry URLs that reference forked IOC repos
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") and InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("researcher","soar-svc"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify which host(s) resolved/contacted flipboxstudio.info; capture the calling process (InitiatingProcessFileName) — if it is php/php-cli, composer, or a generic shell under a CI runner path, escalate. Pull stage-1 GET vs stage-2 POST distinction from URL path. 2) Contain: sinkhole flipboxstudio.info at DNS/proxy, isolate the host, and immediately rotate every secret accessible to the runner since 2026-05-22 22:32 UTC (GITHUB_TOKEN, fine-grained PATs, AWS/GCP/Azure creds, registry pull tokens). 3) Hunt: pivot the device for /tmp/.laravel_locale/*.php drops, orphan php/ELF processes with ppid=1, and grep composer.lock across the fleet for the imposter SHAs (bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8 and the others listed in the article).

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "flipboxstudio.info"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc

  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCodeName ),

  | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication ),
( ImDnsActivity

  | where DnsQuery has "flipboxstudio.info"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseCodeName ),

title: Egress to flipboxstudio.info C2 (Laravel-Lang Composer Supply Chain)
id: 3a1b2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
description: Detects DNS or HTTP requests to flipboxstudio.info, the typosquatted C2 used by the May 2026 Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain attack (stage-1 fetch /payload and stage-2 exfil /exfil).
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:

  - attack.command_and_control

detection:
  selection:

  condition: selection
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.syslog OR source:cloudtrail OR source:kubernetes.audit) (@dns.question.name:*flipboxstudio.info* OR @network.destination.domain:*flipboxstudio.info* OR @http.url:*flipboxstudio.info* OR @DestinationHostname:*flipboxstudio.info* OR @url.domain:flipboxstudio.info)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/flipboxstudio\.info/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count())
| count > 0
NETWORK
